question: True or false: printing a minimum payment on a credit-card bill lowers what people choose to repay?
answer: True. In Neil Stewart's experiment, people shown a minimum repaid less than people shown no minimum at all, and later studies in Britain and the United States found the same pull. A floor meant to guarantee some repayment becomes the number people start from. Real card accounts show payments bunched at the printed minimum.
move: Written minimums turn into targets; pick your number before reading theirs.
trap: Assuming a minimum can only push payments upward.
